settings.ai.subagents: Let the AI use helpers to work in parallel
settings.ai.subagentsDesc: For jobs with several independent parts (reading many sites, comparing items), the AI can hand each part to a helper that runs at the same time and report back. Helpers only read pages and search the web, never click or type, and ask before visiting new sites just as the AI does. Also a button in the sidebar.
settings.ai.subagentModelDesc: Faster and cheaper is the default (for example Claude Haiku, GPT mini or Gemini Flash where your provider has one). Helpers’ tokens count in the chat’s usage.
settings.ai.autoUseDesc: Choose Auto at the top of the model menu and Lumen picks the model for each message on this computer: quick questions go to a small, fast model, hard ones to a stronger one, and a model that is out of usage or not on your plan is skipped. Only the providers ticked here are used. A model you pick yourself is always used as picked.
settings.ai.autoFallback: Switch models automatically when one is unavailable
settings.ai.autoFallbackDesc: Continue with another model you’ve connected when yours is unavailable. The conversation may go to that provider. Off: you get the error and choose.
settings.ai.autoCompactDesc: When a chat nears the model’s limit, its earlier part is summarized instead of dropped. Your messages stay on screen. Type /compact to do it yourself.
settings.ai.cliFullAccess: Give all command-line AIs full access to this computer
settings.ai.cliFullAccessDesc: Sets all four together. Only turn this on if you trust them with your computer: a page they read could try to trick them. Half-way means only some are on. Off by default.
settings.ai.ccUserSettings: Use my Claude Code settings in Lumen chats
settings.ai.ccUserSettingsDesc: Off: Lumen’s Claude Code chats skip your CLAUDE.md, rules, memory and hooks, which saves tokens and startup time. Turn it on if you rely on them, or on proxy or environment settings in ~/.claude/settings.json. Full access always uses them.
settings.ai.claudeCodeFullAccess: Give Claude Code full access to this computer
settings.ai.claudeCodeFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Claude Code’s own tools.
settings.ai.grokBuildFullAccess: Give Grok Build full access to this computer
settings.ai.grokBuildFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Grok Build’s own tools.
settings.ai.antigravityFullAccess: Give Antigravity full access to this computer
settings.ai.antigravityFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Antigravity’s own tools.
settings.ai.codexFullAccess: Give Codex full access to this computer
settings.ai.codexFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first, with its sandbox off. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Codex’s own tools.
settings.ai.grokTerminal: Let Grok Build ask to run terminal commands
settings.ai.grokTerminalDesc: Grok Build in the sidebar can ask to run a command on this computer, and runs it only if you approve. Off: it is told no every time, without asking you. Turning it off can also stop antivirus warnings about Grok’s chat logs.
settings.ai.grokWarmup: Warm up Grok Build when Lumen starts
settings.ai.grokWarmupDesc: Starts Grok Build’s setup in the background so your first message starts faster. Only while Grok Build is connected or chosen; nothing is sent to Grok.
settings.ai.grokKeepConnectedDesc: Each chat that uses Grok Build keeps its own Grok Build running between messages, so replies start sooner. Each one uses about 70 MB of memory while it waits. Messages with images, and Grok Build with full access, still start Grok Build each time.
settings.ai.codexKeepConnectedDesc: Each chat that uses Codex keeps its own Codex running between messages, so replies start sooner and stream as they are written. Each one uses about 80 MB of memory while it waits.
settings.ai.grokKeepIdle: Stop an idle Grok Build, Codex or Claude Code after
settings.ai.grokKeepIdleDesc: A kept Grok Build or Codex, or the Claude Code a chat keeps running between messages, that hasn’t been used this long is stopped; the chat’s next message starts it again. It also stops when its chat’s tab closes or the chat is deleted.
settings.ai.imageGenDesc: When you or the AI ask for a picture, Lumen sends the request to a provider you have already connected that makes pictures, even if the chat is on a model that can’t (Claude, Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex). Automatic tries the chat’s own provider first, then your other connected ones, and moves on if one is out of usage or down; a provider that refuses the picture on content grounds is not retried elsewhere. The picture says which provider made it. Your prompt goes to that provider, and it may count against its usage or your API key’s billing. Lumen never uses a provider you haven’t connected.
settings.ai.researchTabsDesc: Open pages the assistant searches or reads as background tabs in one group, loaded without your logins. Sites where AI is off are never opened.
settings.ai.maxStepsDesc: How many steps the assistant may take on one request before it wraps up. Unlimited still stops if it gets stuck in a loop, and Stop always works.
settings.ai.maxChatRunsDesc: Chats in different tabs can work at the same time. With a limit, once this many are working the next one waits its turn.

settings.unavailable: Settings can only be changed from Lumen's own settings tab. Open ⋯ → Settings.

settings.gmail.setupHelp: Press Sign in with Google and approve read-only access in your browser: there is nothing to set up. If this copy of Lumen has no built-in Google sign-in, or you prefer your own Google Cloud project, open Advanced: in Google Cloud Console, enable the Gmail API, create an OAuth client of type Desktop app, and paste its Client ID and secret there (your own client is then used instead of Lumen’s). Either way Lumen asks only for read-only access to your mail (gmail.readonly), opens Google’s sign-in page in your normal browser, and keeps the tokens encrypted on this computer. The new-tab page only ever receives sender, subject and preview text.
settings.gmail.limits: Because you use your own Google Cloud project, Google’s limits for unverified apps apply: while the project is in Testing, only test users you add can connect, Google shows a “hasn’t verified this app” warning, and the connection ends every 7 days, so you connect again then. Publishing the project removes the 7-day limit.

To keep a repository off the card, don’t give the token access to it.
settings.widgets.github.tokenHelp: Create a fine-grained personal access token at github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens: pick the repositories to include (or All repositories) and grant read-only Issues and Pull requests (Metadata: read is added automatically). No write permissions are needed. Unread notifications work only with a classic token that has the notifications scope, because GitHub doesn’t offer notifications to fine-grained tokens; without one, the card shows the two lists and says so. Stored encrypted by your system; it never reaches the new-tab page and is sent only to api.github.com.

composer.bypass.title: Bypass permissions: the AI doesn’t ask before acting, reading PDFs, using your signed-in accounts or sending what it read anywhere. Click to change this in Settings.
settings.ai.permissionModeDesc: Ask: the AI asks before it acts on a new site, reads a PDF, uses your signed-in account on a site, uploads a file or runs a tool or command. Auto-allow actions: it clicks and types on any site without asking, but still asks about the rest. Bypass permissions: every one of those questions is answered Allow for you, for the sidebar AI on every model and for connected agents, and the chat lists each one as a step (“Allowed automatically”). The AI won’t ask before acting, reading PDFs, using your signed-in accounts, or sending what it read anywhere, so a page it reads could steer it. Still in force: sites where you turned AI off, tabs you keep it off, Hands-off mode, and the rule that it uploads only files you attached or picked. The Choose file… card still waits for you, because Lumen can’t pick a file for you. The model is still told to stop before purchases and sending messages. Background tasks never bypass. Off by default.

settings.ai.agentsNoAsk: Agents in their own window don’t ask
settings.ai.agentsNoAskDesc: A connected agent clicks, types and opens sites in its own Lumen window without asking you first, so it keeps working while Lumen is in the background. Sites where you turned AI off and tabs you keep the AI off are still out of reach. Turn this off to approve each new site.
settings.ai.handsOff: Don’t let the AI act on my pages
settings.ai.handsOffDesc: The AI can read pages you share but won’t click, type or navigate in your tabs, and the Automation server follows the same rule (Settings → Advanced). A command-line AI with full access is not limited.
settings.ai.oneChatPerTabDesc: Off: when you switch to a tab with no chat of its own (a new tab, or one the AI opened), the sidebar keeps your chat, and your next message works in that tab. A tab that already has its own chat still shows it. On: every tab starts with an empty chat.
offers.title: New in this update
offers.later: You can change this any time in {where}.
settings.ai.deviceAccess: Let the AI use files on this computer
settings.ai.deviceAccessDesc: The AI (and agents connected through the Automation server) can look in your folders, such as Desktop and Downloads, upload a file from them to a site you asked it to, and read the clipboard. The first upload to a site in a chat still asks unless you chose Auto-allow or Bypass. Lumen’s own profile, ssh, cloud and keychain folders and .env files stay out of reach.
settings.ai.stayOnMyTab: Never switch away from my tab
settings.ai.stayOnMyTabDesc: The AI keeps working in background tabs and never brings one to the front, even when it would show you a page. The tab you are on stays in view.
settings.ai.closeAiTabs: Close tabs the AI opened when it finishes
settings.ai.closeAiTabsDesc: Off leaves them open. Ask puts the question under the reply. Always closes them when the AI is done, with Undo. Tabs you used or moved yourself stay.

settings.translate.engineDesc: On this device uses Mozilla’s open-source translator (the one in Firefox): private, and works offline once a language pack is downloaded. Your connected AI is the other choice, and the fallback when there is no pack for a language.
settings.translate.autoDesc: On-device translation needs a language pack from Mozilla, about 20 to 55 MB for each direction, downloaded once. Off: Lumen asks before each download.
settings.translate.packs.none: None yet. A pack downloads the first time you translate to or from a language.
settings.translate.offline.registry: Couldn’t reach Mozilla’s list of language packs. Check your connection.
settings.translate.offline.offlineFailed: Couldn’t download: you appear to be offline. Check your connection and try again.
settings.translate.packsDesc: Downloaded from Mozilla, stored in Lumen’s data folder, and used only by on-device translation.
settings.translate.offlineDesc: Get a language’s packs (to and from English) now, so translating works with no connection. Two languages without a pack between them go through English.
translate.error.noSpace: Not enough free disk space for the language pack.
translate.error.registryOffline: You appear to be offline, so Lumen can’t get Mozilla’s list of language packs. Connect and try again.
translate.error.downloadOffline: You appear to be offline, so the language pack couldn’t download. Connect and try again.
translate.error.packRemoved: The language pack was deleted while it was downloading. Try again to download it.
